description:
As an edge computing engineer preparing a configuration file for IoT device deployment, you need to convert the encoding of a specific text file from UTF-8 to ISO-8859-1 (Latin-1). In your /home/user/configs directory, there is a file named device_settings.conf that is currently encoded in UTF-8. 

Your task is to convert /home/user/configs/device_settings.conf from UTF-8 to ISO-8859-1 encoding, overwriting the existing file with the result. After you perform the conversion, verify the change by generating a log file at /home/user/configs/encoding_conversion.log. This log file must contain exactly one line:

Original encoding: UTF-8, New encoding: ISO-8859-1, File: /home/user/configs/device_settings.conf

The automated test will check the presence of the converted file and the exact content of the log file. Do not change the filename of the configuration file. Ensure you do not add extra lines or whitespace to the log file.
truth:
Before the task begins:
- The file /home/user/configs/device_settings.conf exists and is encoded in UTF-8 (contains at least some Latin-1 compatible characters, as well as non-ASCII such as "é").
- The content of /home/user/configs/device_settings.conf before the conversion is:

# Device Configuration
location=São Paulo
temperature_unit=Celsius

After task completion:
- /home/user/configs/device_settings.conf must be converted to ISO-8859-1 encoding, retaining the same text content but encoded in Latin-1.
- The file /home/user/configs/encoding_conversion.log must exist and contain exactly:

Original encoding: UTF-8, New encoding: ISO-8859-1, File: /home/user/configs/device_settings.conf

- No extra whitespace or additional lines are allowed in the log file.
